newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia looks at exporting natgas to Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Colombia looks at exporting natgas to Ecuador.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol is looking at the possibility of exporting natural gas to neighboring Ecuador, a senior executive said in the company's official organ issued Monday.

"We are scheduled to begin an analysis to determine the technical and financial viability of the project," Luis Augusto Yepes, Ecopetrol's vice-chairman of international commerce said in the company's Carta Petrolera magazine.

Ecuador has an annual shortfall in GLP supplies of about 350,000 barrels of crude equivalent and has a 15 percent deficit in terms of the natural gas it needs to generate between 250 and 300 megawatts of electricty, according to Carta Petrolera.

Ecopetrol currently has a contract with Ecuador's Petroecuador to transport 50,000 barrels per day of crude, originally from Ecuador's Lago Agrio field, along its Transandino pipeline for export at the Pacific coast port of Tumaco.

Ecuador is looking to increase the volume by an extra 10,000 barrels per day, much of it heavy crude, which would mean Ecopetrol would have to modify some sections of the pipeline and upgrade pumping stations, used to handling lighter Colombian crude.
